thresholds._note: Thresholds use WHO Air Quality Guidelines 2021 values: PM2.5 interim target 1 = 35, NO2 interim target 2 = 30 and target 3 = 20 µg/m³. The PM10/PM2.5 cut-off of 2 marks a coarse, dust-heavy mix (more than half of PM10 is coarse dust); it is our design choice, not a WHO number.

rules.label: Traffic
rules.when: NO2 is at or above 30 µg/m³
rules.explain: Nitrogen dioxide comes mostly from vehicle exhausts, so high NO2 points to traffic.
actions: Low-emission zones in the city centre

rules.label: Dust
rules.when: PM10 is at least twice PM2.5
rules.explain: Much of the particle pollution is coarse dust, typical of construction, unpaved roads and bare ground.

rules.label: Burning
rules.when: PM2.5 is above 35 µg/m³ while NO2 is below 20 µg/m³
rules.explain: Very fine particles without much traffic gas point to burning: cooking and heating fuels, waste or crop burning.
actions: Support for clean cooking and heating
Enforced bans on open waste burning

rules.label: Cause unclear
rules.when: NO2 or PM10 was not measured
rules.explain: This city did not report NO2 or PM10, so we cannot tell what is driving its pollution.
actions: Expand public air-quality monitoring (NO2 and PM10) and publish the data

rules.label: Mixed sources
rules.when: PM2.5 is above the WHO limit but no single pattern stands out
rules.explain: Pollution comes from several sources at once, often power, industry and regional haze.
actions: A city clean-air plan covering energy, industry and transport
Pushing national government for cleaner power

rules.label: Within the WHO limit
rules.when: PM2.5 is at or below 5 µg/m³
rules.explain: Fine-particle pollution already meets the WHO guideline.
actions: Keep current clean-air policies and protect them in future budgets
